item.description: The COVID-19 pandemic has caused a substantial global health burden, highlighting the need for post-authorization safety evaluation in real-world settings. item.description: Biofilms are spatially structured microbial communities whose architecture, chemistry, mechanics, and cellular states evolve over time. item.title: Effect of intranasal insulin on postoperative delirium: A systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Intranasal insulin probably reduces POD in adult surgical patients. The dose-response findings suggest that 30 IU may provide the greatest benefit, with no apparent additional reduction at higher doses. Larger multicentre trials are needed to confirm the optimal regimen and comprehensively evaluate safety.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: LIR practices in Korea have evolved toward simpler, analyzer-centered workflows; however, variability persists in terms of review criteria, workload, reporting, and reimbursements. Therefore, updated consensus recommendations and reimbursement policies are required.

item.title: Association of serum sodium correction rate with clinical outcomes in adults with hypernatremia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Faster sodium correction was not significantly associated with overall mortality in adults with hypernatremia. However, the observational nature of the available evidence and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicate considerable uncertainty across clinical settings.

item.title: Brainstem enkephalinergic neural circuit underlying cold-induced pain relief in mice
item.description: Application of cold or cold-mimicking chemicals to injury has long been recognized as an effective means of pain relief. However, underlying neural mechanisms remain elusive. item.description: CONCLUSION: iNTS is a major cause of bloodstream infections with the highest burden in children under 5 years of age with susceptibility to the infection amplified by anaemia. The Salmonella serovars involved are increasingly becoming multidrug-resistant, including resistance to critical antibiotics.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Adolescents diagnosed with brain tumors require integrated and developmentally tailored interventions from diagnosis throughout the cancer trajectory. Psychosocial interventions should be based on comprehensive assessments of physical, psychological, and cognitive functioning while also reflecting adolescents' developmental characteristics and individual needs. item.description: CONCLUSION: Pre-pregnancy MASLD was associated with higher risks of offspring neurodevelopmental disorders in analyses without adjustment for maternal BMI and metabolic conditions. item.title: The Modern Cadmus: Reconstructive Surgery and the Human Drive to Restore Form After Fragmentation
item.description: Euripides' The Bacchae dramatizes the devastating consequences of Dionysian ecstasy and the quiet human response that follows. After Pentheus is torn apart by frenzied Bacchae-including his own mother-his grandfather Cadmus gathers the fragmented body and restores its form before burial. This gesture, simple yet profound, reveals a primordial human drive to repair what has been broken. This essay interprets Cadmus as an archetype of the modern reconstructive surgeon. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The refractive EDOF IOL maintains robust astigmatic tolerance comparable to that of the enhanced monofocal IOL, while providing superior intermediate and near vision. However, this extended visual range results in a trade-off with reduced subjective visual quality. These findings highlight the importance of personalized IOL selection based on patients' prioritization of near vision versus photic phenomenon tolerance.

item.description: Background: North Korean defectors (NKDs) are exposed to multiple traumatic events and post-resettlement stressors, placing them at elevated risk for stress-related mental health problems. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Real-world GP-ICI outcomes were comparable between US and South Korean cohorts. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These results suggest that visual, but not auditory, P3b mediates the relationship between past trauma load and social functioning in CHR, suggesting the effect of trauma on the neurophysiological processes subserving visual target detection may contribute to social functioning deficits in CHR individuals.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The association between body mass index and mortality after heart transplantation may differ by sex. The apparent lower mortality among female patients with obesity class I is hypothesis-generating and requires external validation.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Baseline ESR was associated with disease severity and all-cause mortality in dogs with CKD. Baseline ESR may provide complementary prognostic information when interpreted with conventional renal and clinical variables. The ESR-inclusive composite score should be considered exploratory and requires external validation.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with a significant SRB decline in South Korea. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Repeated paper-based PRO-CTCAE assessment was feasible and identified distinct longitudinal trajectories of general pain, joint pain, and fatigue during PAL plus ET.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective pilot study, intraoperative 5-ALA-based PDD was feasible and safe in breast cancer specimens. The addition of fluorescence information may improve diagnostic performance compared with gross assessment alone, although the small number of evaluable cases means that these estimates are exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. Further studies are warranted to determine its clinical utility in breast-conserving surgery.

item.description: Lupus enteritis may precede recognition of systemic lupus erythematosus. item.title: Current status and future prospects of CAR-T therapy for autoimmune diseases
item.description: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy, originally developed for B-cell malignancies, is rapidly being repurposed for severe systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases. The rationale extends beyond suppression of autoantibody production, as B cells also function as antigen-presenting cells, cytokine producers, and organizers of pathogenic immune interactions. item.title: Changes in left atrial reservoir function and their association with exercise capacity after outpatient cardiac rehabilitation in early-stage heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In early-stage HFpEF, LA reservoir function increased after outpatient CR, and changes in LA reservoir function were independently associated with changes in exercise capacity.

item.title: Postoperative ctDNA in Resectable Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: From Molecular Residual Disease Detection Toward Risk-Adapted Adjuvant Therapy and Surveillance
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative ctDNA provides complementary molecular risk information beyond conventional pathology in resectable ESCC. However, prospective MRD-guided trials are required before postoperative treatment or surveillance strategies can be routinely modified on the basis of ctDNA results alone.

item.description: CONCLUSION: The WTC method is an effective strategy for reducing blood leakage after pulmonary artery division with automatic staplers.

item.description: The restricted mean time (RMST) up to a given time horizon has increased in popularity due to its more direct interpretation in terms of average time alive. item.description: Upland rice is cultivated in dry and rain-fed fields and is grown primarily in regions with limited water resources. Due to the development of irrigation systems and the comparatively lower yield and eating quality of upland rice relative to paddy rice, its cultivated area has decreased in Japan over the years. item.title: Eye contact facilitates faster responding but does not modulate gaze cueing of attention
item.description: Eye contact attracts attention and facilitates subsequent social interaction. However, previous studies have reported mixed findings regarding its influence on gaze cueing, leaving the replicability and robustness of this effect unclear. These inconsistencies may partly reflect methodological differences across studies: some have compared direct gaze with vertically averted gaze, whereas others have used closed eyes as the control condition. item.title: Multiple mechanisms of rhythm switching in recurrent neural networks with adaptive time constants
item.description: Although recurrent neural networks (RNNs) trained on cognitive tasks have become a widely used framework for studying neural computation, the internal mechanisms by which RNNs switch between rhythms across multiple frequency bands, and how these mechanisms relate to neuronal time constants, have not been systematically analyzed. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Primary GP5 was associated with unfavorable oncological outcomes in low-volume de novo mHSPC treated with upfront ARPI-based doublet therapy. Its prognostic significance and potential role in guiding treatment intensification require further validation.

item.title: Self-reported eating speed and the risk of breast cancer among Japanese women: a retrospective cohort study from the LIFE Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: In this large cohort, slower self-reported eating speed was associated with a modestly lower risk of incident breast cancer. By providing one of the first large-scale longitudinal evaluations of the association between self-reported eating speed and breast cancer risk, this study addresses a gap in epidemiological evidence but does not establish that slower eating prevents breast cancer.

item.title: Pharmacotherapy for older adults with cancer: a digest of the Japanese clinical practice guidelines (2nd edition) - lung cancer
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These guidelines provide practical, evidence-based recommendations for pharmacotherapy in older adults with lung cancer. They emphasize individualized treatment strategies based on patient characteristics, treatment goals, and tolerability. Further research in older populations is required to strengthen the evidence base for geriatric oncology.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: An immune-active tumor microenvironment characterized by high T-cell receptor diversity, CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, and M1 macrophage enrichment was associated with favorable ICI responses in MPM. item.title: A barcode-enabled distance-based paper sensor using silver chloranilate for semi-quantitative determination of chloride in various water sources
item.description: Chloride monitoring is important for drinking-water quality assessment, corrosion control, and environmental analysis. item.description: Various rodent paradigms have been developed to study early-life adversity and stress-related changes in maternal care, but many rely on external stress procedures or disruption of the dam-pup environment. item.description: Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers, including colorectal and pancreatic cancers, remain among the most lethal cancers worldwide. item.title: Giant left atrial thrombi despite surgical left atrial appendage resection in rheumatic heart disease: a case report
item.description: BACKGROUND: Although surgical left atrial appendage resection reduces a major source of thromboembolism, left atrial cavity thrombosis may still occur in patients with persistent severe atrial stasis.

item.title: A transformer-based deep learning model for predicting the use of atherectomy devices during PCI from preprocedural cardiac computed tomography angiography
item.description: CONCLUSION: A Transformer-based deep learning model using preprocedural CCTA showed clinically relevant performance for predicting atherectomy device use during PCI in an independent external test cohort. These findings suggest that the model may support lesion assessment and procedural planning.

item.description: The nematode Caenorhabditis elegans is a widely used model organism, yet its infrared (IR) spectroscopic characterization has been limited by motion and strong water absorption in the mid-infrared region. item.description: Liquid crystals (LCs) based on π-conjugated building blocks are well-established platforms for engineering soft optoelectronic materials. item.description: Neuroligins (NLGNs) organize neuronal connectivity by engaging a diverse set of interaction partners, yet how extracellular recognition couples to intracellular growth programs remains unclear. item.title: Mechanical force orchestrates inflammatory and apoptosis-associated signaling in periodontal tissues during orthodontic tooth movement using complementary in vivo and in vitro models
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Orthodontic force induces inflammatory responses and alters mitochondrial apoptosis-associated signaling in periodontal tissues. These findings highlight potential interactions between inflammatory pathways and apoptosis-related molecular events during OTM. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: POS tobacco advertising exposure remains common in Japan, and young children are still exposed to tobacco marketing. Mandatory regulation of POS tobacco advertising should be implemented to protect children from early exposure to tobacco marketing.

item.description: BACKGROUND: Single fetal demise (sFD) in monochorionic (MC) twins may lead to acute exsanguination through placental anastomoses and result in brain injury in initially surviving cotwins. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: IABP innovation has focused on balloon catheter design, pressure sensing, and adaptive control to improve hemodynamic support and counterpulsation accuracy. item.description: CONCLUSION: These multidisciplinary European guidelines offer a comprehensive and evidence-based framework for the diagnosis and management of ODS. They are intended to promote standardized, high-quality care across Europe and to improve outcomes and quality of life for individuals affected by this complex condition. item.description: Andes virus (ANDV) causes hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), with rare outbreaks involving person-to-person transmission. item.title: Introduction of contraceptive implants as a family planning strategy in Honduras and Chiapas: Results from the Salud Mesoamerica Initiative (SMI)
item.description: Expanding access to a broad range of contraceptive methods is critical for reducing unintended pregnancies and improving reproductive health. This study evaluates the introduction of subdermal contraceptive implants in the selected areas of Honduras and Chiapas, Mexico, in the context of the Salud Mesoamérica Initiative, a results-based financing program focused on disadvantaged populations. item.title: Mutation-induced structural and dynamic perturbations at the IL-17A-IL-17RA interface: Therapeutic insights from multi-replicate molecular dynamics simulations
item.description: The interaction between Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) and its receptor IL-17RA plays a key role in pro-inflammatory signal transduction and is implicated in the pathogenesis of inflammatory autoimmune diseases. Blocking this protein-protein interaction is a major approach to developing therapeutic agents to inhibit IL-17A-induced signaling. item.title: Effectiveness of childhood pneumonia awareness program among pregnant women: A hospital based quasi experimental study
item.description: CONCLUSION: The findings highlight the program's effectiveness and emphasize the importance of regularly promoting similar awareness campaigns as a strategy to improve maternal and child health. Educational programs play a crucial role in empowering mothers to take timely preventive measures, thereby reducing pneumonia-related risks in children under five. Regular promotion of such campaigns is recommended to maintain and enhance maternal and child health.

item.title: Association of unmet discharge needs on readmission or mortality among acute respiratory failure survivors during the COVID-19 pandemic: The Addressing Post-Intensive Care Syndrome (APICS-COVID) multicenter prospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Across six US academic hospitals during the COVID-19 pandemic, we did not detect a significant association between higher and lower unmet healthcare needs and 3-month readmission or mortality. Compared to APICS-01, unmet follow-up appointments increased but readmission and mortality decreased. Home health services, durable medical equipment, and medications remained robust during pandemic conditions.
